provenance.notes: Mid-size rfq kit for general contractors chasing owners, developers and architects, and managing subcontractor bid lists. Leaned on sector portfolios, preconstruction and prequalification. Least sure about the owner project portal and preconstruction estimator ranges, which depend on their cost history and project systems.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Project pages for healthcare, education, industrial, office fit-out, retail, hospitality and multifamily, each with size, delivery method, schedule, value band as supplied and the architect named with permission
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners and architects shortlist a construction company that has built their kind of building, and they want facts, not a photo gallery.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Budgeting, constructability review, value engineering, scheduling, and how design-build, construction management and lump-sum delivery differ, with when to bring the contractor in
pageStructurePlus.why: Developers pick a general contractor early when preconstruction is explained. That's where the negotiated work comes from.

pageStructurePlus.section: Trade subcontractor registration and plan room
pageStructurePlus.contains: Trade subs register their trades, regions and size, see open bid packages, and download plans and specs after sign-in, with the GC's bid instructions
pageStructurePlus.why: Good subcontractors are scarce. A GC that makes bidding easy gets more and better trade numbers, which wins the job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Safety programme, [bonding capacity] and insurance as placeholders, licences held, financial reference request, project references and a one-step pack request
pageStructurePlus.why: Institutional owners and developers prequalify before inviting. A ready pack keeps the contractor on their invitation lists.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Principals, project managers and superintendents, each with the projects they've run, sectors and how to reach the right one
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners hire the team, not the logo. Showing the superintendent who ran the last hospital job wins the next one.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How the firm phases work in operating hospitals, schools in session and open retail: site logistics, after-hours work, dust and noise control, infection-control procedures as the firm supplies them
pageStructurePlus.why: Renovation owners fear disruption most. A construction firm that explains how it protects occupants gets the renovation shortlist.

designDirections.name: Fit-Out Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Contractors focused on tenant fit-out and renovation who need enquiries from tenants, brokers and landlords
designDirections.headlineSample: Office and retail fit-out in {City}, on schedule
designDirections.whyItFits: Butter & Denim's geometric display type and friendly blue suit a fit-out contractor selling speed and clarity to tenants, not committees.

designDirections.name: Sector Book
designDirections.bestFor: Mid-size commercial builders showing project facts by sector to owners, developers and architects
designDirections.headlineSample: Commercial construction across {City}, sector by sector
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Its tabular, mono-labelled cards make each project's size, delivery method and schedule readable at a glance.

designDirections.name: Landmark
designDirections.bestFor: Established general contractors selling signature buildings to developers, institutions and design-led owners
designDirections.headlineSample: Building {City}'s landmarks since our first project
designDirections.whyItFits: Gallery White was made for portfolios. Didone heads and white space let finished buildings carry the page the way architects present work.

openers.line: Your portfolio is a gallery of finished buildings with no size, delivery method or schedule. An owner's rep shortlisting general contractors wants those facts beside each project.
openers.hook: Open their projects page and check whether any project lists size, sector, delivery method or schedule.
openers.linkLine: Projects with the facts owners compare: {demo-link}

openers.line: Hospitals, warehouses and office fit-outs all sit in one construction gallery on your site. A school board's facilities director wants to see the schools you built, and only those.
openers.hook: Count how many sectors share their portfolio page and whether there's a filter.
openers.linkLine: A portfolio by sector, one page each: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find anywhere for a subcontractor to register with {Business Name} or see open bid packages. More trade numbers on bid day usually means a sharper construction price.
openers.hook: Look for a subcontractor, vendor or bid opportunities page. If there's none, or only an email, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A subcontractor registration and plan room page: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Hiring supers with no careers page
openers.line: Saw you're hiring a superintendent and an assistant project manager, but the site has no careers page. Experienced supers check a contractor's project list before they take a call.
openers.hook: Find their job posts on job boards or social profiles, then confirm what the site says about careers.
openers.linkLine: A construction careers page with the project list behind it: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site doesn't say a word about the safety programme. Institutional owners score a general contractor's safety before they read the proposal.
openers.hook: Search the site for safety. Never state their record; only note that the programme isn't shown.
openers.linkLine: A safety programme page owners can read: {demo-link}

openers.line: An owner who wants your prequalification documents has to email and wait. Developers building an invitation list usually move on to the construction firm whose pack is a click away.
openers.hook: Check whether a prequal or capability pack is downloadable, request-only or missing.

openers.line: Your project photos are beautiful but large, and the site crawled on my phone. Developers often check a builder between meetings on a phone.
openers.hook: Load their portfolio over mobile data and note how long the first project takes.
openers.linkLine: The same portfolio, fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site lists preconstruction as a service with no explanation. Developers who want a design-build partner early want to know how you budget and when to bring you in.
openers.hook: Find their services page and check what it says about preconstruction or delivery methods.

openers.line: Most of your recent posts are office and retail fit-outs, but the site talks about ground-up construction. Tenants and their brokers looking for a fit-out contractor wouldn't guess.
openers.hook: Scroll their recent posts and count fit-out projects. Name building types, not tenants.
openers.linkLine: Fit-out work on its own page: {demo-link}

openers.line: An architect commented that your team kept the design intact through value engineering. That's what the next design team wants to read before recommending a general contractor.
openers.hook: Read comments on their posts and any public recommendations. Copy one phrase from an architect or owner.
openers.linkLine: Architect and owner comments beside the projects: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Award or topping-out not on site
openers.line: Congratulations on the topping-out you posted. The site still shows the same projects as before, so owners who check you this month won't see it.
openers.hook: Find a recent award, topping-out or completion post and check whether the site has the project.
openers.linkLine: That project on a construction project page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You build out of several offices, but the site has one contact page. An owner in your second region can't tell which construction team would run their project.
openers.hook: Compare offices on their listings and posts with the site's contact page.
openers.linkLine: A page per office with its project team: {demo-link}

openers.line: School and campus owners plan renovations around the long break, and they shortlist general contractors months before. The firms with school projects on show get the invitations.
openers.hook: Use this a few months before the long school break in their region.
openers.linkLine: Education construction projects on their own page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site shows the buildings but not the project managers and superintendents who built them. Owners hire the commercial construction team that will be on site.
openers.hook: Look for a team or leadership page. Note whether PMs and supers appear, or only principals.
openers.linkLine: Project leadership with the jobs they ran: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is fine commercial construction. It deserves a project page with the facts an owner's rep can forward to their board.
openers.hook: Pick their newest project post and name it: building type, sector and what stands out.
openers.linkLine: That project with its facts on one page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a strong commercial project.

I went through the {Business Name} site and couldn't find project facts by sector, a prequalification pack, or a place for subcontractors to register. I put together a sample with all three, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it to you and whoever leads business development?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my note got lost under bid day. Here's the sample for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has project pages by sector with size and delivery method, a preconstruction section, an owner prequalification pack and a subcontractor plan room. If it isn't useful, tell me and I'll stop.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites and bid tools for general contractors around {City}. I sent you a note a couple of days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with project pages by sector, a prequalification pack for owners and a subcontractor plan room, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Should it go to you or to business development?"

IF YES:
"What did you and the team think?"
 → let them talk, note who else decides: principals, BD, preconstruction
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, changes and adding projects. For a contractor your size I'd quote about {Build Price}."
"Could we take thirty minutes with you and your BD lead this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a scope and a deposit invoice. We start with the sector pages, since that's what owners read."

objections.objection: Our work is relationships and negotiated deals.
objections.handler: "Then the site is what your relationships forward. When a developer you know sends your name to their board, they open the sector page first."

objections.objection: We can't name clients or show values.
objections.handler: "Most construction project pages describe the building, size, delivery method and schedule without naming the owner or the price. Anything named needs written clearance."

objections.objection: We use a plan room service already.
objections.handler: "Keep it. The site gives subs a front door with your instructions and registration, then links to the plan room you already use."
"Understood. I'll send a one-page summary for the principals, and walk them through the demo together whenever suits."

objections.objection: We just redid the site a few years ago.
objections.handler: "Then keep the brand. I rebuild the parts owners and subs use, sector projects, prequal and the plan room, and leave the rest alone."

objections.objection: We have more work than we can staff.
objections.handler: "Then the site helps you choose. Sector pages bring the work you want, and a careers page backed by the project list helps you hire the supers to build it."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's sector project pages, preconstruction, a prequal pack and a subcontractor plan room. That's a fraction of one general conditions line."

email.subject: Sector projects and prequal for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for general contractors in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name} with project pages by sector and a prequalification pack for owners. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} construction demo down on Friday.

If you or your BD lead want it up longer, one word is enough.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — owners around {City} are setting next year's capital projects and invitation lists about now. Thought of you.

The construction site with sector projects and the prequal pack is still here, same price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a small fraction of one project's general conditions, not to a marketing budget.
Price sector pages by project count, because each project needs facts and owner clearance.
Quote the prequalification pack and subcontractor registration early; owners and subs use them first.
Anything reading from their project or accounting systems is a separate software project.
Expect principals, business development and preconstruction to sign off; allow two review rounds.
Never publish a bonding limit, safety rate, licence or project value the contractor hasn't supplied in writing.

lineItems.description: Max with several projects, each carrying size, delivery method, schedule, team and cleared photos.
Max with gated documents, version dates, a financial reference request step and notification to business development.

lineItems.item: Subcontractor registration and bid package page
lineItems.description: Max with trade and region registration, sign-in to open packages, bid instructions and links to the plan room.
Max with a page per delivery method, a budget enquiry form and a cleared preconstruction case example.
Max with many PMs and superintendents, each linked to the projects they ran and filtered by sector.
Max with the region's team, projects, licences held there and its own enquiry routing.
Max with roles by office, a field and office track, a short application and a feed of open jobs.

whatElseYouSell.name: Construction progress photo and drone days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Monthly site visits for progress photos and aerials give the owner updates and build the construction project page as it goes, with the owner's permission."
whatElseYouSell.when: From the start of each notable project, cleared with the owner.

whatElseYouSell.name: Owner and architect outreach by sector
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each month, a short note to developers, facility directors and architects in one sector, with a project like theirs and the prequal pack link."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once sector pages are live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Proposal and interview presentation design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A proposal template and shortlist interview deck that match the site, so the general contractor looks the same from website to final interview."
whatElseYouSell.when: Before their next big shortlist interview.

whatElseYouSell.name: Award submission writing
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Construction award entries written from the project page facts and photos, cleared by the owner and architect before they go in."
whatElseYouSell.when: Two months before the regional builders' awards deadline.

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite signage and hoarding graphics
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Site signs and hoardings that carry the project, the team and the careers address, seen by everyone passing a busy construction site."
whatElseYouSell.when: At mobilisation on each visible project.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profiles for each office
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each office's profile kept current with completed projects and hiring posts, so 'commercial construction company near me' finds the right team."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, after office pages go live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Project completion case studies
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Plain write-ups of how the team phased an occupied hospital wing or recovered a fit-out schedule, cleared by the owner."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, after a project with a story the owner will clear.

whatElseYouSell.name: Owner and architect reference collection
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After each building handover, the owner and architect get a short request for a quote about the general contractor, approved before it goes up."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trade subs who bid your construction packages have sites that don't help them get invited elsewhere. A GC recommending its web person is a favour they remember."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Subs want to stay on the GC's list and trust its recommendations.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The architects you build for need sector portfolios too. A general contractor's introduction after a good project carries weight."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Architects and GCs share owners and recommend vendors to each other.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tenant reps who send you fit-out work need listing and tenant guide pages. Your introduction gets me to their marketing lead."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Brokers value the fit-out contractor that makes their tenants happy.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The owner's reps who run your bigger construction jobs sell to the same institutions and have thin sites. A GC's referral opens the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Owner's reps and GCs work side by side and trade introductions.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The ready-mix and steel suppliers on your jobs sell to every builder in the region with a brochure site. Your purchasing manager's introduction helps."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers want to keep a big construction account and trust its vendors.

withoutAI.route: Facility management firms taking over at handover
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The facility firm that takes over your finished buildings needs a service request page for occupants. Your handover introduction starts it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Facility firms meet the GC at every handover and value a good word.

withAI.pitchLine: "Subs drop in the GC's bid package, and the assistant lists their trade scope and exclusions to price, so more construction numbers arrive on bid day."
withAI.whyItWorks: Subs bid more of the GC's packages, which sharpens the client's prices.

withAI.pitchLine: "It drafts spec sections from the architect's past projects and notes for their specifier to review, so construction documents come out cleaner."
withAI.whyItWorks: Architects save drafting time, and the GC gets clearer documents to build from.

withAI.pitchLine: "Tenant reps enter space size and finish level and get a rough fit-out budget range from the contractor's own past projects, with a GC enquiry button."
withAI.whyItWorks: Brokers answer tenants' first question fast, and the enquiries go to the client.

withAI.pitchLine: "It turns the GC's monthly construction reports into a one-page summary for the owner's board, for the rep to edit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Owner's reps rewrite reports every month; this saves them the hours.

withAI.route: Quote desk assistant for material suppliers
withAI.pitchLine: "Builders email material schedules, and the assistant drafts the supplier's quote with lead times for the sales desk to check."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster supplier quotes keep the GC's construction schedule on track.

withAI.route: Handover manual reader for facility firms
withAI.pitchLine: "Technicians ask about a system in the new building and get the answer from the contractor's handover manuals."
withAI.whyItWorks: Facility firms inherit thick manuals nobody reads; this makes them useful.

softwareAI.name: Owner enquiry routing to preconstruction
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every owner or developer enquiry gets an instant reply and lands with the right preconstruction lead by sector and region."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30, once the enquiry forms are live. Needs preconstruction leads and their sectors.

softwareAI.name: Subcontractor bid invitation sender
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Registered subs get invitations to construction bid packages that match their trade and region, with reminders before bid day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, once subcontractor registration is live. Needs bid packages and dates.

softwareAI.name: Subcontractor prequalification portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Trade partners upload safety, insurance, licences and references once, and estimators see which subs are approved before they invite."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their current prequal form, approval rules and who signs off.

softwareAI.name: Bid package scope splitter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads the drawings and specs and drafts trade bid packages with scope, inclusions and exclusions for the construction estimator to finish."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past bid packages and the documents they came from. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sub proposal comparison assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Trade proposals arrive in every format; it lines them up against the scope and flags missing items so the estimator levels bids faster."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a few past bid days with the proposals and the leveling sheets. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bid leveling sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sub numbers, scope gaps and plugs side by side for every trade on bid day, saved with the construction bid for later."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their current leveling spreadsheet and an estimator to test.

softwareAI.name: Qualifications and RFP response writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It drafts responses to owner RFPs from the firm's own project pages, team profiles and past proposals, for business development to edit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once sector pages and profiles exist. Needs past winning proposals. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Owner project portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners log in to see the construction schedule, progress photos, budget status and decisions they owe, for every project with the GC."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs where schedules, photos and budgets live today and a project to pilot.

softwareAI.name: Superintendent daily report from voice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The super records a few minutes at the end of the day, and a daily report with trades on site, work done, weather and delays lands in the project file."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their daily report format and a superintendent to try it. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: RFI and submittal log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every RFI and submittal on the construction project with who owes the answer, how long it's been out and what it holds up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their current logs and the architects' turnaround expectations.

softwareAI.name: Weekly owner progress report sender
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each Friday, owners get a short progress note with photos and the coming week's construction work, assembled from the daily reports."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the daily reports. Needs owner contacts and the PM's approval step.

softwareAI.name: Punch list app with photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the building, tap the item, take the photo, assign the trade, and the owner sees the punch list close out before handover."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a project nearing completion and the trades' contacts.

softwareAI.name: Meeting minutes drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owner-architect-contractor meetings become draft minutes with decisions and action owners for the construction PM to approve and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a few past minutes and permission to record meetings. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Subcontractor insurance certificate chaser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sub insurance certificates are tracked against expiry, and the trade gets reminders before the GC has to stop them coming on site."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, with the prequal portal. Needs current certificates and expiry dates.

softwareAI.name: Preconstruction budget estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Early budgets by building type, size and finish level from the contractor's own past project costs, for preconstruction to adjust."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs cost history from a set of finished projects, organised by building type.

softwareAI.name: Lessons-learned search across projects
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A PM asks what went wrong on the last lab building and gets the firm's own close-out notes, RFIs and change orders on that construction type."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs close-out reports and project files in one place. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Project pipeline and backlog dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pursuits, bids out, awards and backlog by sector and office on one screen, so the principals see next year's construction work taking shape."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs their pursuit list, bid log and current backlog.

softwareAI.name: Change event narrative drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Site notes, RFIs and photos about a change become a draft change order narrative for the construction PM to price and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past change orders and the documents behind them. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Field staff certification matrix
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which superintendents and foremen hold the safety and site certifications each construction project requires, and who's due to renew."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the field staff list and their certifications.

softwareAI.name: Public tender and invitation watcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads public tenders and owner invitations every week and shortlists the construction projects that fit the contractor's sectors, size and region."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the portals they watch and the work they want. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the subcontractor prequal portal for GCs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a subcontractor prequal portal for one general contractor. Every mid-size GC chases the same insurance certificates by email."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first GC paid for it; every GC has the same sub paperwork.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Builders' exchange plan room and member pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give members a plan room front door and a company page each, so GCs post bid packages and subs find them in one construction directory."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exchanges sell membership on access to bids and need modern member tools.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member general contractors a sector portfolio and prequal pack template as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one agreement reaches many builders.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every builder you invite submits prequal documents and bids through one portal tied to your development pipeline."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: You built the contractor side already; the developer sees the same paperwork from the owner's side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The hospital system, university or school authority
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Facilities leadership sees every capital construction project's schedule, budget and contractor in one place, fed by the GCs' own reports."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Institutions run many projects at once and the owner portal you built is the prototype.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each regional contractor in your group gets sector pages, prequal and a plan room on one frame, under its own name owners know."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups keep local brands and want one system, and each firm is a repeat build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs builders and starts from a blank page. License the sector portfolio, prequal and sub registration frame."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client; the project data structure is what took longest to get right.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Same GC kit in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New general contractor clients in a new region
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one general contractor per sector in each metro. {City}'s is signed; the next metro is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the build, the pitch and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Surety and bond brokers' contractor clients
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer your contractor clients a prequalification pack page and backlog dashboard that make their bonding reviews easier."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokers keep clients by helping them grow bonding capacity, and clean reporting helps.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Joint design-build pages for each architect and builder pairing, with shared projects and one enquiry form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Design-build teams pitch together and need one place that shows the partnership.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your GC clients want owner portals and sub prequal that read from the project system you set up. I build the outward-facing side."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Consultants get asked for portals they don't build, and the contractor client is proof you can.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The GC with a half-built tool
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Half-built owner portals and sub databases are common among general contractors. I finish them, because I've shipped the same construction workflow for another builder."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy and need someone who knows the workflow.

upsellLadder.offer: General contractor site build plus care, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: The principals approve the demo and scope.
upsellLadder.line: "The site and the care plan sit on one contract, so a finished project or new office is an email to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first owner and developer enquiries arrive through the sector pages.
upsellLadder.line: "Owners are enquiring from the sector pages. Routing each one to the right preconstruction lead keeps the construction conversation warm."

upsellLadder.trigger: Subs are registering, and estimators still invite them by hand.
upsellLadder.line: "Subs are signing up. Sending construction bid invitations by trade and region gets you more numbers on bid day."

upsellLadder.trigger: A sub shows up on site with expired insurance, or prequal paperwork backs up.
upsellLadder.line: "That expired certificate is what a prequal portal catches before the sub reaches the construction site."

upsellLadder.trigger: BD mentions several owner RFPs due in the same month.
upsellLadder.line: "Your RFPs keep landing together. A writer drafts from your own project pages so BD edits instead of starting blank."

upsellLadder.trigger: An owner asks for more frequent updates, or a repeat client wants a login.
upsellLadder.line: "That owner wants to see progress without asking. A portal shows the construction schedule, photos and decisions they owe."

upsellLadder.trigger: Year-end planning shows the principals can't see next year's backlog by sector.
upsellLadder.line: "Planning next year is guesswork without the pipeline in one view. Let's put pursuits, bids and construction backlog on one screen."
